ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Preventive Visit — Lorraine Hansberry

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual
code.originalText: Periodic adult preventive visit during chemotherapy after surgery

text.paragraph: Periodic adult preventive visit, on day 10 of the first cycle of chemotherapy after surgery. [S]

Ms. Hansberry, now 33, comes for her yearly preventive visit on day 10 of the first cycle of fluorouracil, leucovorin and irinotecan after her pancreaticoduodenectomy. The cycle went well: one day of nausea settled with olanzapine, two loose stools on day 4 controlled with loperamide, and no fever. She takes pancrelipase three capsules with meals and two with snacks, and her stools are formed. Insulin glargine is 10 units at night; fasting readings are 110 to 140 mg/dL with no low readings. She takes apixaban twice a day without bleeding. The tingling in her fingers in the cold is fading now that oxaliplatin has stopped. She writes most mornings and has finished a draft of the new play's second act. Her PHQ-9 today is 5. [S]

tr.td: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma after six cycles of modified FOLFIRINOX and pancreaticoduodenectomy (R0); on chemotherapy after surgery; diabetes due to pancreatic disease on insulin; exocrine pancreatic insufficiency on pancrelipase

Fluorouracil, leucovorin and irinotecan every two weeks; pegfilgrastim; apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily; insulin glargine 10 units; pancrelipase; pantoprazole; olanzapine, ondansetron and loperamide as needed; oxycodone rarely

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-21; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 52.4 kg, BMI 19.7; blood pressure 106/66
Head, eyes, ears, nose, and throat
No mouth sores; no scleral icterus
Examined with her agreement and a chaperone: no mass, skin change or nipple discharge; no axillary nodes
Regular rhythm; no murmur; no leg swelling
Healed upper midline and right subcostal incision; soft, non-tender; no mass, no fluid
Port site clean; no rash or bruising
Monofilament sensation normal; pulses present; no lesions
Light touch slightly reduced at the fingertips; vibration and reflexes normal; steady gait

Epigastric pain for about two months, boring through to the back and worse after meals and lying flat, with nausea, early fullness, a loss of 5 kg (8 percent of her weight), and pale, loose stools: an upper abdominal cause such as a bleeding ulcer or a pancreatic or duodenal tumor must be found. Upper endoscopy and pancreas-protocol CT booked this week
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to the documented collapse in pain and the account of a suspected duodenal ulcer. Superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.
Iron deficiency anemia from chronic upper gastrointestinal blood loss: black stools on and off for three weeks, two near-fainting spells, hemoglobin 9.1 g/dL, MCV 74 fL, ferritin 6 ng/mL
S — Synthetic finding anchored to the documented account that she was told she had anemia and bleeding ulcers.

New hyperglycemia: A1c 6.6% and random glucose 132 mg/dL in a lean woman of 32 who is losing weight; new diabetes with weight loss can be the first sign of a pancreatic cancer, so it is to be confirmed and explained, not labeled type 2
S — Synthetic finding; superseded when diabetes due to the pancreatic cancer was recorded at the second visit.

Adenocarcinoma of the head of the pancreas, 3.1 cm, invading the duodenum, borderline resectable (tumor contact of more than half the circumference of the superior mesenteric vein, no arterial contact), no distant spread, CA 19-9 486 U/mL after biliary drainage; on EUS-guided biopsy; synthetic modern detail linked to her documented cancer, whose primary site the sources record differently
S — Synthetic histology, site, stage and course; the sources say she died of cancer and differ on whether it was pancreatic, duodenal, or colonic with spread to the pancreas (R). See sources.md.
Diabetes due to the pancreatic cancer (pancreatogenic, type 3c): A1c 6.6% at intake and fasting glucose 141 mg/dL
S — Synthetic consequence of the synthetic tumor.
Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency from obstruction of the pancreatic duct: pale, floating, loose stools after fatty meals and weight loss
S — Synthetic consequence of the synthetic tumor; diagnosed clinically, as guidance allows in pancreatic cancer.
Cancer-related pain in the upper abdomen and back, 6 out of 10, with sleep broken by it
S — Synthetic symptom of the synthetic tumor.
Obstruction of the distal common bile duct by the tumor, relieved by a covered metal stent placed at ERCP
S — Synthetic consequence of the synthetic tumor.

Chemotherapy-induced diarrhea from irinotecan, grade 2 (five to six watery stools a day above her usual), starting on day 3 of cycle 5, with low potassium and magnesium and mild dehydration; no fever, blood or neutropenia; resolved
S — Synthetic treatment effect; not a historical claim.

Oxaliplatin peripheral neuropathy, grade 1: tingling in the fingers and toes in the cold, lasting a few days after each cycle, with mild tingling at the fingertips between cycles; no effect on writing or buttons
S — Synthetic common effect of oxaliplatin.
After pylorus-preserving pancreaticoduodenectomy with superior mesenteric vein resection: loss of the head of the pancreas, with more marked exocrine insufficiency and insulin-requiring diabetes
S — Synthetic consequence of the synthetic operation.

Periodic adult preventive visit completed. Health risk assessment reviewed and the prevention plan updated for a woman of 33 in treatment for pancreatic cancer. Cervical screening is due (last test four years ago, normal); she prefers to have it after chemotherapy ends, which is reasonable. Influenza and COVID-19 vaccines given today, between cycles; no live vaccines during chemotherapy. Hepatitis B surface antibody was negative before chemotherapy, so hepatitis B vaccination is due after chemotherapy, when the response will be better. Contraception was discussed again: estrogen-containing methods are not advised because of her clot risk; condoms for now, and a copper or levonorgestrel IUD if she wants one later. [S]

First cycle of fluorouracil, leucovorin and irinotecan tolerated well. Surveillance after treatment will be with history, examination, CA 19-9 and CT every three to six months for two years. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 30 minutes, with her consent, building on her conversations with the palliative care team. She named a health care agent, recorded in the confidential part of the chart and not named here, and completed a health care proxy form. She said that she wants to be told everything about her illness directly and in plain words, never through someone else; that she wants all treatment that has a real chance of controlling the cancer, as long as she can think clearly and write; and that if the cancer returns and can no longer be controlled, she would want care focused on comfort and on time at her desk and with her friends, at home if possible, rather than intensive care. She asked that her pain be treated fully even if it makes her sleepier near the end. To be revisited at each change in her health and at least yearly. [S]
